title: Microsoft 365 Copilot connectors: custom icons and display names for custom connectors
summary: Hold: the checklist starts at an admin-center tab without explaining how to reach it, and the delegated Graph permissions omit the requirement for an administrator to be signed in. The roadmap facts and rename API are supported, but the statement that the feature performs no autonomous actions needs narrowing.

claims.claim: The roadmap plans adding or customizing custom Copilot connector icons through Graph or the Microsoft 365 admin center.
claims.quote: Add or Customize icons for Custom Copilot connectors using the Graph API or from the M365 Admin Center.

claims.claim: The roadmap plans adding or customizing custom Copilot connector display names through Graph or the Microsoft 365 admin center.
claims.quote: Add or Customize display names for Custom Copilot connectors using the Graph API or from the M365 Admin Center.

claims.claim: Custom Copilot connectors bring a developer's external data sources into Microsoft 365 experiences through Microsoft Graph.
claims.quote: Custom connectors allow you to integrate your own data sources into Microsoft Graph to bring external data into Microsoft 365 experiences.

claims.claim: The roadmap product is Microsoft Copilot (Microsoft 365).
claims.quote: "products": ["Microsoft Copilot (Microsoft 365)"]

claims.quote: "targetDate": "September CY2025"

claims.quote: "previewDate": null

claims.claim: The roadmap release phase is General Availability.

1. Add or Customize icons for Custom Copilot connectors using the Graph API or from the M365 Admin Center.

claims.claim: Prebuilt connectors show standard connector names and icons in the Copilot Search data source filter.
claims.quote: Prebuilt connectors display standard connector names and icons as data sources.

claims.claim: SDK-built custom connectors show the developer-supplied connection name and icon in the data source filter.
claims.quote: For custom connectors built with the Copilot connectors SDK, the connection name and icon that the developer supplies is displayed as the data source.

claims.where: What's changing; Why it matters; Scope: Connectors
claims.claim: API-built custom connectors show a default connection name and icon in the data source filter.
claims.quote: For custom connectors built with the Connectors API, a default connection name and icon are displayed as the data source.

claims.claim: The FAQ directs API-built custom connector display-name and description changes to Update externalConnection.
claims.quote: To change the display name or description for a custom connector built with the Connectors API, see Update externalConnection.

claims.claim: The FAQ advises SDK connector developers to set their intended name when publishing.
claims.quote: If you're using the Copilot connectors SDK to build your custom connectors, be sure to set the name that you want when you publish your connector.

claims.where: controls[0].api; Governance controls; Governance guidance: At rollout
claims.claim: PATCH /v1.0/external/connections/{connectionsId} updates a connection's name and description through the request body.
The name property is the connection display name shown in the Microsoft 365 admin center.
claims.quote: name | String | The display name of the connection to be displayed in the Microsoft 365 admin center. Maximum length of 128 characters.

claims.claim: The connection name has a maximum length of 128 characters.
claims.quote: Maximum length of 128 characters.

claims.claim: The Graph update request body can set the connection description.
claims.quote:
The following properties can be updated.
 description | String | Description of the connection displayed in the Microsoft 365 admin center.

claims.where: controls[0].note; Risk assessment: Security & identity; Governance guidance
claims.claim: ExternalConnection.ReadWrite.OwnedBy is the least-privileged permission for the connection update API.
claims.quote: Application | ExternalConnection.ReadWrite.OwnedBy | ExternalConnection.ReadWrite.All

claims.where: controls[0].note; Risk assessment: Security & identity; Governance guidance
claims.claim: ExternalConnection.ReadWrite.All is the higher-privileged permission for the connection update API.
claims.quote: Delegated (work or school account) | ExternalConnection.ReadWrite.OwnedBy | ExternalConnection.ReadWrite.All

claims.claim: The Graph update call uses application or delegated permissions, without a stated administrator requirement for delegated access.
claims.quote: Allows the app to read and write settings of external connections on behalf of a signed-in user. The signed-in user must be an administrator. The app can only read and write settings of connections that it is authorized to.
claims.fix: Replace the Graph sentence in Scope with: 'The Graph update call supports application permissions or delegated work-or-school permissions; for delegated access, the signed-in user must be an administrator (row 1).' Cite https://learn.microsoft.com/graph/permissions-reference#externalconnectionreadwriteownedby.

claims.claim: Apps granted the update permissions can rename the connections covered by those permissions.
claims.quote: The app can only read and write external connections that it is authorized to, or it can create new external connections.
claims.fix: Add https://learn.microsoft.com/graph/permissions-reference#externalconnectionreadwriteownedby to sources to support the permission-scope statement.

claims.claim: A documented admin-center route for editing the display name and description of an API-built custom connection was not found.
claims.quote: Searched: custom Copilot connector icon display name Microsoft 365 admin center edit; site:learn.microsoft.com/microsoft-365/copilot/connectors custom display name edit. Opened FAQ, manage-connector and enhance-copilot-discovery; found API update guidance but no custom API-built editing route.

claims.where: controls[1].ui; controls[1].api; Governance controls; Open questions
claims.claim: No admin UI or API operation for setting an API-built custom connection's icon was found.
claims.quote: Searched: custom Copilot connectors configure icons Graph API connectorId Teams app manifest icon; custom connector icons admin center; site:learn.microsoft.com/graph connector icon custom. Opened FAQ, manage-connector, SDK overview, externalConnection v1.0/beta and searchSettings; no API-built icon setter.

claims.claim: The externalConnection resource reference lists no icon property in v1.0 or beta.
claims.quote: Searched: Graph externalConnection icon; custom Copilot connectors configure icons Graph API. Read Properties and JSON representation at graph/api/resources/externalconnectors-externalconnection?view=graph-rest-1.0 and ?view=graph-rest-beta; neither lists an icon property.
claims.fix: Add https://learn.microsoft.com/graph/api/resources/externalconnectors-externalconnection?view=graph-rest-1.0 to sources; the briefing currently cites only the beta resource reference for its two-version absence claim.
